skill.name: github-actions-templates
skill.description: Create GitHub Actions workflow templates for testing, Docker builds, Kubernetes deployment, matrix builds, reusable workflows, and security scans.
skill.summary: Generate practical GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow patterns for common application delivery tasks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static detections are mostly false positives from Markdown code fences, template paths, and GitHub Actions secret placeholders. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or skill runtime command execution was found in SKILL.md. One semantic issue remains: security scan examples use mutable third-party action refs that should be pinned.

remediation.suggestion: Pin external GitHub Actions to stable version tags or commit SHAs and review updates regularly.
Prefer GitHub OIDC role assumption for AWS deployments and document required repository permissions.
Mark example URLs, clusters, secrets, and deployment commands as placeholders requiring user review.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Third-Party Action References
semantic_findings.description: The security scanning workflow uses third-party actions from mutable master branches. Those refs can change without review and execute code in CI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template directly shows external actions using @master refs. This is a known CI supply-chain risk and is not covered by the static hardcoded URL finding.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable CI/CD workflows without rebuilding common patterns from scratch. This skill provides GitHub Actions templates for tests, builds, deployments, scans, approvals, and reusable workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates Node.js test workflows with dependency caching and coverage upload steps.
Provides Docker image build and publish workflows for GitHub Container Registry.
Shows Kubernetes deployment workflows with cloud credential setup and rollout checks.
Builds matrix workflows for multiple operating systems and language versions.
Documents reusable workflow patterns for shared test jobs and required secrets.
Includes examples for security scans, production approvals, and Slack notifications.
limitations: Templates require adaptation for each repository, package manager, cloud account, and deployment target.
The skill does not validate secrets, permissions, runner policies, or protected environment settings.
Examples are not a substitute for security review of production CI/CD pipelines.
Referenced asset files are mentioned, but only SKILL.md was present in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI for application teams
use_cases.description: Create repeatable test, lint, and coverage workflows for repositories that need consistent GitHub Actions practices.

use_cases.title: Prepare deployment workflows
use_cases.description: Draft build, container publish, Kubernetes deploy, approval, and notification workflows before platform review.

use_cases.title: Teach workflow patterns
use_cases.description: Explain matrix builds, reusable workflows, permissions, caching, and secret usage through concise workflow examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic test workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions test workflow for my Node.js project. Include install, lint, test, caching, and pull request triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a workflow that builds a Docker image, publishes it to GitHub Container Registry, and uses least-privilege permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Kubernetes deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production deployment workflow for Kubernetes with protected environments, rollout checks, and safer cloud authentication guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor into reusable workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CI/CD requirements and propose reusable GitHub Actions workflows for tests, builds, security scans, and deployments.

output_examples.input: I need CI for a Node.js repository with linting, tests, and coverage upload.
output_examples.output: A test workflow plan with pull request triggers, Node version matrix, dependency caching, lint checks, test execution, and coverage publishing.

output_examples.input: I need to publish container images when a version tag is pushed.
output_examples.output: A release workflow outline with checkout, registry login, metadata generation, Docker build caching, image publishing, and minimal package permissions.

output_examples.input: I need safer production deployment steps for Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan with protected environments, cloud authentication guidance, kubeconfig setup, rollout verification, and notification steps.

best_practices: Pin third-party actions to stable tags or commit SHAs before using workflows in production.
Set explicit job permissions and use protected environments for production deployments.
Review every generated command, secret, runner, and deployment target before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not copy templates without adapting package managers, paths, cloud roles, and environment names.
Do not use broad repository token permissions when a job only needs read or package access.
Do not store long-lived cloud keys when OIDC role assumption is available.

faq.question: Does this skill create complete GitHub Actions files?
faq.answer: It provides workflow patterns and templates that can be adapted into repository workflow files.

faq.question: Can it support Docker image publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Docker build and publish pattern for GitHub Container Registry.

faq.question: Can it design Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Kubernetes deployment steps, rollout checks, and cloud credential setup guidance.

faq.question: Does it validate my repository secrets?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify secret names, values, permissions, and environment protection settings.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production pipelines?
faq.answer: It is a starting point for production workflows, but each pipeline needs review and testing.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
